cause: The earlier VEX32 public-plan reader reduced targeted AVX32 scan instructions but was attached inside shared initial legacy readers. GCC13 ordinary scan/batch costs and some SIMD64 costs increased, so the reader was held.
change: Reuse the source-validated VEX2 plan generator and reader at one existing cold generic-fallback call boundary. Keep the generic function, initial scalar readers, call ABI and all feature/adapter routing. Only exact CS_MODE_32 bare C5 prefixes after extension rejection are eligible; every other path calls the existing generic implementation.
isolation: Clang-only prototype. A separate code section holds the new fallback selector and a separate read-only section holds its generated plans. GCC and scan-adapter builds retain the original implementation. Preserve all previous negative evidence.
semantic_owner: Plans are regenerated from the current canonical opcode and operand tables, including pp/L, ModR/M groups, reserved-vvvv policy and immediate extents. One existing generator owns every generated variant including reduced tables.
gates: Require complete records and mode/vendor protected-page coverage, current source generator reproducibility, unchanged non-decoder runtime objects, and inspect ordinary decoder text identity except the one call target. Only then collect compiler costs and actual throughput.
